Introduction

Pennsylvania licenses Home Care Agencies and Home Care Registries to provide non-medical services. The PA Department of Health oversees licensing under the Home Care Agencies and Home Care Registries Act (Act 69).

Table of Contents

  • Understand Pennsylvania’s Regulations
  • Choose the Type and Size of Agency
  • Business Structure and Licensing
  • Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan
  • Establish Operations Infrastructure
  • Hire and Train Qualified Staff
  • Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans
  • Marketing and Community Outreach
  • Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections
  • Frequently Asked Questions

1. Understand Pennsylvania’s Regulations

PA DOH licenses home care agencies and registries under 28 Pa. Code Chapter 611. Requirements include licensing, background checks, training, and quality standards.

2. Choose the Type and Size of Agency

Choose between a Home Care Agency (employs caregivers) or Home Care Registry (refers independent contractors). Services include personal care, homemaker, and companion services.

3. Business Structure and Licensing

Register with the PA DOS, apply for home care agency or registry license, and secure insurance.

4. Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan

Pennsylvania benchmarks: Private pay rates $22-$32/hour, Medicaid waiver rates $17-$24/hour, break-even 12-18 months.

5. Establish Operations Infrastructure

Set up office, scheduling, and documentation systems.

6. Hire and Train Qualified Staff

PA requires background checks (Act 34, Act 151, FBI) and training per DOH standards.

7. Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans

Develop policies meeting PA DOH requirements under Act 69.

8. Marketing and Community Outreach

Build networks in Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, and communities statewide.

9. Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections

Maintain licensing and comply with Act 69 requirements.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between an agency and registry? An agency employs caregivers; a registry refers independent contractors.
